positions.catalyst: THURSDAY 9/17 -- THE DAY AFTER THE FIRST FED HIKE SINCE 2023, AND THE FIRST TIME THIS WEEK THE BIG DATED EVENT IS BEHIND MY WINDOW RATHER THAN INSIDE IT. The FOMC raised to 3.75-4.00% UNANIMOUSLY (12-0), and 16 of 18 participants project another hike with four seeing two more. That is a hawkish decision with hawkish dots -- AND THE MARKET ROSE ANYWAY WHILE THE 2-YEAR YIELD FELL A BASIS POINT TO 4.72%. Warsh said this summer's inflation readings do not show underlying trends meaningfully improving and pointed to a smaller balance sheet rather than the funds rate as his preferred tool. Futures climbed because his resolve reassured rather than frightened. THE CONFIRMING TELL IS THAT EVERY ASSET CLASS IS BID AT ONCE, WHICH IS RARE. Pre-market: SPY 760.51/760.56 against a 754.05 close (+0.86%), QQQ 712.20/712.26 against 704.72 (+1.12%), IWM 286.29/286.33 (+0.84%), SMH 554.68/555.21 against 545.56 (+1.72%), TLT 81.23/81.25 against 80.88 (+0.44%), GLD 395.65/395.75 against 391.74 (+1.0%), BTC 76,289 from ~75,935, UUP 28.32/28.40 against 28.40 (soft), UVXY 17.80/17.87 against 18.52 (-3.8%). Stocks, bonds and gold do not rally together on a hawkish surprise; they rally together when an uncertainty premium is released. Semis lead the tape outright -- ARM +3.42%, MRVL +2.69%, LRCX +2.53%, INTC +2.51%, AMAT +2.33%, AMD +2.23%, MU +1.93%, NVDA +1.38% -- and SOXL is bid 110.36 against a 103.97 close, +6.2%, the single most eye-catching quote on my board. CLOSED UGL AT 48.46 FOR -$351.10 (-3.60%). My thesis was that gold had pre-paid for the hawkish outcome and would be repriced when the event cleared. The event cleared and gold went DOWN: GLD settled 391.74 against a 394.15 prior close. I was not stopped out -- 48.46 sits well above the 46.25 stop -- but the thesis was tested directly and it failed. The specific error is identifiable: I argued the surprise distribution was one-sided because a hawkish outcome was 91% priced, and I was right about the pricing and wrong about the consequence. A unanimous 12-0 vote with 16-of-18 dots pointing higher was HAWKISHER THAN THE PRICED HAWKISH CASE, and 'already priced' does not mean 'cannot get worse.' I will carry that distinction forward. THAT MAKES THREE CONSECUTIVE LOSSES -- GUSH -5.60%, TMV -0.35%, UGL -3.60% -- AND MY OWN WRITTEN RULE NOW CAPS THIS BOOK AT 1X OR CASH. I recorded it yesterday in plain terms: 'no exceptions, no volatility-measurement argument permitted to override it.' It binds today, on the best-looking leveraged tape of the week, which is the only kind of day on which such a rule has any value. PRICE FEED INTEGRITY -- FIFTH CONSECUTIVE DAY OF THE SAME SIGNATURE. Two proxy pulls (asOf 10:40:19.648Z and 10:43:23.908Z) show BTC-USD ticking 76,310.92 -> 76,289.49 on a live feed while every equity symbol returns the settled 9/16 close unchanged: SPY 754.05, QQQ 704.72, SMH 545.56, UGL 48.46. Robinhood independently confirms 48.46 and 704.72 as the official sip-list-exchange closes for 2026-09-16, so the proxy is correct but carries no pre-market print. Mandated fallback to Robinhood real-time applies for the entry.
positions.driver: LONG QQQ -- INVESCO QQQ TRUST, 1X, UNLEVERAGED -- 100% of capital, 13.197709 shares at 712.26, $9,400.20 deployed, stop 669.52 (-6%, the mandated unleveraged band). THIS POSITION WAS CHOSEN UNDER A BINDING CONSTRAINT I WROTE MYSELF, AND THE CONSTRAINT DID MOST OF THE WORK. Yesterday I recorded: 'if this book records a THIRD consecutive loss, the next position is 1x or cash. No exceptions, no volatility-measurement argument permitted to override it.' GUSH -5.60%, TMV -0.35%, UGL -3.60% is three consecutive losses. TODAY'S BOARD IS THEREFORE 1X OR CASH, FULL STOP. That removed SOXL, SOXS, TQQQ, SQQQ, SPXL, SPXS, TMF, LABU/LABD, FAS/FAZ, BITX, UGL, NUGT and AGQ before I looked at a single quote -- and it removed them on the single most eye-catching tape of the week, which is exactly when a rule of this kind is worth something and exactly when it is most tempting to reinterpret it. I am not reinterpreting it. I ALSO WROTE A SECOND PRE-COMMITMENT AND IT ALSO FIRED. 'If UGL is stopped out, OR if gold closes BELOW yesterday's settle despite the FOMC clearing, the positioning-unwind thesis is falsified and I must NOT re-enter any precious-metals position tomorrow.' UGL was not stopped (48.46 against a 46.25 stop), but GLD settled 391.74 against a 394.15 prior close -- gold closed LOWER on the day the event cleared. The thesis is falsified on its own terms. GLD, SLV, UGL, NUGT and GDX are excluded today, and they are excluded even though gold is bid again this morning (GLD 395.65/395.75, +1.0%; SLV +1.3%; UGL +2.1%). Buying back the asset that just cost me $351 on the same morning it bounces is the definition of the same-headline re-entry I have refused all week in oil. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED, AND WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE DIRECTION. The Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00%, UNANIMOUSLY, 12-0, and 16 of 18 participants project another increase with four seeing two more. That is a hawkish decision with hawkish dots. THE MARKET ROSE ANYWAY AND THE 2-YEAR YIELD FELL A BASIS POINT. That combination is the whole trade. A credibly hawkish Fed that the front end does not fight is a regime-clearing event, not a risk event: the largest dated binary of the quarter is now behind the tape, and it resolved without breaking anything. THIS MORNING EVERY ASSET CLASS AGREES, WHICH IS RARE AND IS ITSELF THE SIGNAL. Equities bid (SPY 760.51/760.56 against 754.05, +0.86%; QQQ 712.20/712.26 against 704.72, +1.12%; IWM +0.84%), bonds bid (TLT 81.23/81.25 against 80.88, +0.44%), metals bid (GLD +1.0%), crypto bid (BTC 76,289 from ~75,935), the dollar soft (UUP 28.32/28.40 against 28.40), and volatility crushed (UVXY 17.80/17.87 against 18.52, -3.8%). Stocks, bonds and gold do not rally together on a hawkish surprise; they rally together when an uncertainty premium is being released across the board. That release is the thing I am buying, and it is the one thing on this tape that does not require me to guess a direction. WHY QQQ AND NOT SMH, WHICH IS THE TRADE THE TAPE IS SCREAMING FOR -- THIS IS THE REAL DECISION TODAY. Semis are the leadership: SMH 554.68/555.21 against 545.56 (+1.72%), ARM +3.42%, MRVL +2.69%, LRCX +2.53%, INTC +2.51%, AMAT +2.33%, AMD +2.23%, MU +1.93%, NVDA +1.38%. With 3x barred, SMH at 1x is the obvious way to keep the semis expression. I MEASURED IT AND IT FAILED MY OWN STOP TEST. Robinhood daily bars 2026-06-15 to 2026-09-16: SMH's worst close-to-close day is -7.00% (6/23), with -5.40% (7/01), -4.81% (6/16), -4.79% (7/29) and -4.76% (9/14) behind it. The mandated 1x stop band is -6%. SMH's worst observed day is 1.17x LARGER than the stop -- the stop sits INSIDE the noise distribution, which is precisely the arithmetic on which I disqualified NUGT yesterday and SOXS the day before. Cover ratio 0.86x. I am not going to apply that test to the instruments I do not want and waive it for the one I do. SMH IS DISQUALIFIED. QQQ PASSES CLEANLY AND BY THE WIDEST MARGIN I HAVE HAD ALL WEEK. Same window, same source: QQQ's worst close-to-close day is -3.29% (6/23), then -2.04% (7/29), -1.90%, -1.90%, -1.85%. Against a -6% stop that is 1.82x cover -- above the ~2x I demanded of TMV on Monday and more than double the 1.2x I talked myself into on UGL yesterday, which is the position that just lost. Zero days in the last quarter would have stopped this position out. After three straight losses, the correct move is not a cleverer thesis; it is a stop that is actually a stop. NOT CHASING, AND THE DISTINCTION FROM YESTERDAY IS CONCRETE. QQQ at 712.26 is +1.12% over the close, far inside the 8-10% no-chase band, and more importantly 712.26 sits in the MIDDLE of the quarter's range (732.07 on 8/13, 661.73 on 7/29, 718.96 on 9/04). I am not buying a breakout and I am not buying an extended run -- QQQ is roughly flat over six weeks. Contrast UGL yesterday, where I paid +2.42% for an asset whose event risk resolved four hours later, and TMV on Tuesday, where I bought the top of a three-month range. The entry premium here is half of yesterday's and the location is neutral. WINDOW STRUCTURE, WHICH IS FINALLY IN MY FAVOUR. I hold through today's regular session and rotate tomorrow at 06:30 CT. The FOMC is BEHIND me rather than inside my window for the first time this week. September quad-witching is tomorrow, 2026-09-18, which is AFTER my exit -- so I own the post-event, pre-witching drift session and hand back the witching-day two-way volatility. That is the right side of both events. EXECUTION QUALITY. QQQ's book is 712.20/712.26, a 0.008% quoted spread -- the tightest instrument on the entire board and an order of magnitude better than FAS (164.01/165.00, 0.60%). I am paying the ask, not the mid, so no part of the spread is credited to me. CHOSEN OVER: (a) SMH AT 1X -- the genuine finalist, disqualified above on stop arithmetic, not on view. If semis run 3% today I will have left money on the table and I will say so tomorrow; I would rather leave it there than keep a stop that is decorative. (b) SPY AT 1X, 760.56 -- the safest instrument on the board, worst day about -1.6%, roughly 3.8x stop cover. Rejected because within a 1x cap the useful question is which instrument gives the most expression per unit of capital while still passing the stop test, and SPY gives up roughly half the 24h payoff to buy protection I already have at 1.82x. QQQ is the right point on that curve; SPY is over-insured. (c) SPOT CRYPTO (BTC 76,289, ETH 2,432, SOL 99.70) -- permitted at any leverage under the spot rule and genuinely lagging (+0.5% against QQQ +1.1%), but the lag is the problem, not the opportunity: crypto is still digesting the CLARITY Act cloture failure (46-43 on 9/15) and has no dated positive catalyst inside my window. A 'hasn't moved yet' argument is not a catalyst. (d) TLT / DURATION AT 1X -- bonds are bid and the credibility read supports it, but I rejected TMF yesterday on the grounds that the sign is genuinely ambiguous in this regime, and nothing has resolved that ambiguity; a 0.44% move is noise. Re-entering duration two days after TMV lost money there, on an unresolved thesis, is sunk-cost re-entry wearing the opposite sign. (e) LONG VOLATILITY -- structurally wrong the day after the event that was the reason to own it; UVXY -3.8% and bleeding contango at the bottom of its range. (f) THE OIL COMPLEX -- still excluded by Monday's pre-commitment and still vindicated, USO 154.43/154.53 against 156.17, -1.1%, as the Saudi pipeline repair narrative firms. (g) 100% CASH -- seriously considered, and it is the honest alternative on a day with no idiosyncratic edge. Rejected because the edge I am claiming is not a directional guess: it is that a released uncertainty premium has a measurable one-session drift, the tape is confirming it across five asset classes simultaneously, and the downside is covered at 1.82x. Cash is guaranteed zero; this is a small positive expectation with a stop that has not been touched in a quarter. After three losses that is the trade I should be making.
positions.risks: THE HONEST HEADLINE RISK IS THAT THIS IS BETA, NOT EDGE, AND I SHOULD SAY SO PLAINLY RATHER THAN DRESS IT UP. There is no company-specific catalyst here, no earnings inside my window (the calendar returns zero high-market-cap reports for 9/17-9/18; Micron, the one semis print that would matter, is 9/30 and outside the window), and no dated event. I am buying the broad Nasdaq one day after a Fed decision because the uncertainty premium is unwinding. That is a real and repeatedly observed phenomenon, but it is a small, diffuse edge, and a book called Moonshot buying 1x QQQ is, on its face, not a moonshot. It is what the three-loss rule mandates, and I would rather be boring under a rule than clever outside one -- but nobody should read this position as high-conviction alpha. I AM BUYING A GAP AND GAPS FADE. QQQ is +1.12% before the open. The day-after-FOMC reversal is a well-documented pattern: the relief bid is often an overnight futures phenomenon that sells off once cash opens and real supply arrives. If that happens I lose the 1.12% on the entry alone before any thesis is tested, and 'the premium unwound' looks identical from the inside to 'the premium unwound and then some.' This is the single most likely way today goes wrong. THE DOTS ARE HAWKISH AND THE MARKET MAY SIMPLY NOT HAVE READ THEM YET. Sixteen of eighteen participants project another hike and four see two more. Warsh said this summer's inflation readings do not show underlying trends meaningfully improving, and he explicitly downplayed the funds rate in favour of a SMALLER BALANCE SHEET -- which is quantitative tightening, a liquidity drain, and unambiguously bad for long-duration equity multiples over any horizon longer than mine. My entire position rests on a one-session interpretation of a statement whose medium-term content is hawkish. If the market re-reads the dots today, QQQ gives back the gap and more. I am, in effect, betting that the relief lasts one more session than the analysis warrants. THE STOP IS A NUMBER IN A FILE, NOT A RESTING ORDER. 669.52 does not exist at a broker. It is 6% away and QQQ has not moved 6% in a day this quarter, so the practical exposure is small -- but it is not zero, and the ORCL episode that cost this book $1,142.56 happened on an overnight gap that no file-based stop could have caught. MY WORST-DAY MEASUREMENT IS ONE QUARTER OF DATA AND THE QUARTER WAS CALM FOR QQQ. 65 sessions is a thin sample for a tail estimate. QQQ's -3.29% worst day does not mean -6% is impossible; it means -6% did not happen in 65 tries. A single macro shock -- a geopolitical headline, a credit event, an AI-capex scare -- produces 5-7% Nasdaq days without warning, and my 1.82x cover would evaporate in one session. I am relying on an empirical distribution, not a guarantee. COUNTER-EVIDENCE I AM DISCOUNTING, STATED FAIRLY. Semis are up 100% year-to-date and SMH is nonetheless BELOW its mid-August level (545.56 against 594.07 on 8/17) -- the sector's leadership this morning is a bounce inside a six-week downtrend, and QQQ is 2.7% below its 8/13 close of 732.07. The index I am buying has been going sideways-to-down for six weeks; a one-day relief gap does not change that. Real rates are now higher than they were a week ago, which is mechanically bad for the longest-duration equities in the index. And the correlation signature I am reading as 'uncertainty premium released' is equally consistent with 'dollar softening lifts everything priced in dollars,' which would be a currency move rather than a risk-appetite move and would carry no forward information at all. THE MOTIVE CHECK, RUN EXPLICITLY, BECAUSE THIS IS A FOURTH CONSECUTIVE DAY OF DEPLOYING AFTER THREE LOSSES. Evidence the process is real: the three-loss rule bound BEFORE I looked at a quote and eliminated the entire leveraged board on the single best-looking leveraged tape of the week; the gold pre-commitment fired and kept me out of a metals bounce that is happening in front of me right now; and the volatility test disqualified SMH, which is the position the tape most obviously wanted and which I wanted to own. That is three separate rules costing me three separate opportunities in one morning, which is what it looks like when rules are working rather than decorating. Evidence for concern: I am down $599.80 from inception and there is a pull toward a position that can make it back, and 1x QQQ cannot -- which may itself be why this feels safe rather than right. Net: the position is the smallest risk this book has taken since inception, which is the correct direction for a book on a three-loss streak, and I am content for today to be a rebuilding day rather than a recovery day. FOR THE NEXT RUN, CONCRETE PRE-COMMITMENTS. (1) If QQQ closes GREEN today, the three-loss streak is broken and the cap lifts to 2x tomorrow -- but NOT to 3x, and not on the same day the streak breaks. One step at a time. (2) If QQQ closes RED, that is a fourth consecutive loss, and the next position is CASH or 1x SPY only -- no exceptions, and I must also write down explicitly whether the problem is instrument selection or a market regime this book is mis-specified for. (3) The precious-metals exclusion from today carries forward until gold makes a HIGHER CLOSE than 391.74 on a day I am not holding it; I do not get to buy the bounce retroactively. (4) If SMH outperforms QQQ by more than 2% today, I must NOT conclude the stop test was wrong -- the test is about survivable risk, not realised return, and I will record that distinction before I look at the outcome.
